messages.content: What is the effect of economic status on happiness levels?

function.name: get_happiness_index
function.description: Fetches the happiness index for a given country or area based on data compiled from global surveys. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

country.description: The country for which to retrieve the happiness index.

year.description: The year for which to retrieve the happiness index.

demographic_group.description: The demographic group for which to retrieve the happiness index. If not specified, the total for all groups will be returned.

We can provide a general explanation, referencing research like the Easterlin paradox, the diminishing returns of income on happiness, etc. We might also want to provide some data. We could use the get_happiness_index function to fetch happiness indices for different income groups for a specific country and year. But the question is general. We could ask for a specific country and year. But maybe we can provide a general answer with references to studies. We could also mention that happiness tends to increase with income up to a point, after which additional income has diminishing returns. Also mention that relative income matters more than absolute. Also mention that low-income individuals may experience lower happiness due to stress, but high-income individuals may have higher happiness due to security, but also potential for social comparison. Provide some data: e.g., in the US, high-income earners report higher life satisfaction than low-income earners. Provide a table of happiness index by income group for a few countries.
